name: Space weather
description: NOAA Space Weather Prediction Center watches, warnings and alerts, the G, S and R scales, Kp and flux series, GNSS error and timing holdover, and decisions scored by the clocks that matter: grid operating procedures applied before storm onset and time source failover before holdover expires. For any organization that has to operate through a geomagnetic storm, a radiation storm or a radio blackout: utilities, telecom, aviation, farms, rail, ports and satellite operators.
outsideParties: the NOAA Space Weather Prediction Center
the FAA and ICAO space weather centers

advisorRoles.name: Space weather forecaster (SWPC liaison)
advisorRoles.description: Explains the products, what a level means, what changed between messages and how uncertain the arrival time is.

advisorRoles.name: Reliability engineer (grid advisor)
advisorRoles.description: Knows the operating plan elements, which entities must be told and what the log must show.

glossary.definition: NOAA levels 1 to 5 (Minor to Extreme) for geomagnetic storms (Kp), solar radiation storms (10 MeV proton flux) and radio blackouts (X-ray class).
G1 is Kp 5, G2 is 6, G3 is 7, G4 is 8 (including 9-), G5 is 9.
R1 is M1, R2 is M5, R3 is X1, R4 is X10, R5 is X20.
S1 is 10 particle flux units at 10 MeV and above; each level is ten times the one before.
A watch is elevated risk with uncertain timing; a warning is an event occurring, imminent or likely; an alert says a threshold has been crossed.
Geomagnetically induced current in a transformer neutral, driven by the geoelectric field in V/km.

productConventions: SWPC products carry a message code (for example WATA20, WARK05, ALTK06, SUMX01) and serial number, and times are UTC.
A geomagnetic storm watch lists the highest level predicted for each day; copy real layouts, not invented thresholds.
Grid procedure notices follow NERC EOP-010: information received, actions at predetermined conditions, a termination condition, and evidence in logs.
Impact messages state effects and actions, not solar physics; partner messages agree on severity and duration.
Exercise products are marked as exercises; a simulated level is never presented as an NOAA product.
realismRules: Scale levels describe potential effects; impacts are regional and depend on latitude and ground conductivity.
CME arrival time is uncertain by hours; state the lead time the scenario assumes.
A flare gives minutes of effect and no lead time; radiation lasts hours to days; scintillation can last days after the peak.
Satellite navigation is degraded for hours at G4 and days at G5; HF is intermittent at G3 and may be lost for a day or two at G5.
Do not give engineering advice about protection settings or radiation doses.
Real storms are historical and dated; fictional events use invented utilities, satellites and places.
